image_description: A close-up, low-angle view of a staircase featuring a modern metal bannister system. The image shows stone or concrete steps ascending diagonally. A sleek, tubular metal handrail runs parallel to the stairs, supported by thin vertical metal balusters and a diagonal cable/mesh infill structure. To the left, there is a darker wooden structural element or secondary railing that appears somewhat disjointed from the main metal assembly.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The dark wooden beams/railing on the left side exhibit nonsensical geometry. They appear to float or merge into the background without clear connection points, and the perspective lines do not align logically with the rest of the scene.
The end of the lower handrail appears to melt or fuse ambiguously into the step/riser area rather than terminating in a defined cap or return. The connection point lacks physical clarity.
The texture of the stone steps is overly smooth and plastic-like in areas, lacking the expected micro-detail and wear patterns of real stone, suggesting AI smoothing.

alignment_reasoning: The image strongly conforms to the 'bannister' class. All testable checkpoints regarding geometry, functional components (handrail/balusters), and materials are present and accurate. The only untestable checkpoint was the newel post due to framing. The visual representation of a modern metal balustrade is taxonomically correct.
artifact_reasoning: While the main metal railing is structurally sound, significant artifacts degrade the quality. The wooden structure on the left suffers from structural collapse and illogical geometry (severity 3.5). Additionally, the handrail termination at the bottom shows fusion issues (severity 2.5), and step textures appear artificially smoothed. These errors prevent a high artifact score despite good class alignment.
